newsitem.title: USA: Texas Panhandle cattle late off $2 at $71 - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Texas Panhandle cattle late off $2 at $71 - USDA.

text.p: Feedlot cattle markets in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma areas turned active late Wednesday, with a burst of sales at $71.00 per cwt, down $2.00 from last week's top, according to feedlot sources and USDA.
About 13,500 head traded in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area after 1500 CT, USDA said.
Packers had been bidding $71.00 since Monday, with cattle owners hanging onto asking levels mostly at $73.00.
However, weakness in boxed beef prices and losses in CME live cattle futures Wednesday probably spurred the late sales, market sources said.
"I think people really started getting nervous when the board (CME live cattle futures prices) fell," one feedlot manager in the Texas Panhandle said.
Beef prices at Wednesday's close were quoted down $0.23 to $0.76, with 294 fabricated loads sold, according to USDA.
October live cattle futures settled off 0.600 cent a lb at 71.425 cents.
